description:
Surface and delta tracking are two independent programs with disjoint signatures and zero shared code, and both duplicate the power iteration (transport_csg.rs:300-412 vs keff_delta.rs:623-692).

This is a rewrite of both, not a refactor. Retire the duplicated power iteration in the same change. Also unify the two incompatible source samplers (SourceBox rejection at transport_csg.rs:303-326 vs domain.sample_point at keff_delta.rs:634).

Note the delta path has NO Tally at all - zero hits in keff_delta.rs - so tally consistency across methods is part of this.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
DESIGN FINDING, from reading both loops (2026-09-17). This is smaller than 'a rewrite of both', and here is why.

The surface loop (transport_csg.rs:709-980) is:

    locate -> path
    sigma_t = local
    d_bound = distance_to_boundary(path)
    d_col   = -ln(xi)/sigma_t
    score track-length over min(d_col, d_bound)
    if d_col < d_bound { COLLIDE }   else { cross surface }

The COLLIDE block is lines 769-950, about 180 lines -- fission/capture/inelastic/n2n/elastic, URR draws, MF=6 sampling, the lot. It is ALREADY method-independent: it takes a position, a material and an energy and does physics. Delta tracking does not change any of it.

So surface and delta differ in EXACTLY ONE quantity: how far to the next REAL collision, and in which material. Everything else -- tallying, banking, the boundary crossing, the leak accounting -- is common.

That makes the unified loop a dispatch on  computing , with the existing branch and the existing collision block untouched:

    Surface          -> d = -ln(xi)/sigma_t,  material = path.material
    Delta{majorant}  -> bounded_delta_flight(..) (landed in d08b3fc7bd)
                          Collision{position, material} -> collide there
                          Exit{position}                -> re-locate, continue
                          Exhausted                     -> leak

NOT a 180-line extraction, and not two drivers merged by hand.

THE ONE REAL SUBTLETY, which is the actual work: the delta arm needs distance to the edge of the DELTA REGION, which is not distance_to_boundary -- that returns the nearest surface at ANY coordinate level. It needs the boundary of the cell that DECLARED delta, i.e. the level in GeometryPath where  was set. So locate should report that level alongside the method, and a distance_to_boundary variant should be able to stop at a named level.

That is a small, well-defined addition to op-867c.1's work rather than a new subsystem.

SECOND ITEM, independent: the delta path has no Tally at all (zero hits in keff_delta.rs). Under the design above that solves itself -- tallying happens in the shared part of the loop, on the segment actually streamed -- but it needs checking that a delta segment's track-length contribution is scored on the RIGHT segment, since a delta flight crosses several materials virtually before its real collision. Score per sub-flight, not per real collision.

(Superseding a previous comment on this bead that the shell mangled.)

The surface loop (transport_csg.rs:709-980) is:

The COLLIDE block is lines 769-950, about 180 lines -- fission, capture, inelastic, (n,2n), elastic, URR band draws, MF=6 sampling. It is ALREADY method-independent: it takes a position, a material and an energy, and does physics. Delta tracking changes none of it.

So surface and delta differ in EXACTLY ONE quantity: how far to the next REAL collision, and in which material. Tallying, banking, boundary crossing and leak accounting are all common.

That makes the unified loop a dispatch computing (d_col, collision_material), leaving the existing branch and the existing collision block untouched:

    Surface           -> d = -ln(xi)/sigma_t, material = path.material
    Delta{majorant}   -> bounded_delta_flight(..), landed in d08b3fc7bd
                           Collision{position, material} -> collide there
                           Exit{position}                -> re-locate, continue
                           Exhausted                     -> leak

NOT a 180-line extraction, and not two drivers merged by hand.

THE ONE REAL SUBTLETY, which is the actual work: the delta arm needs the distance to the edge of the DELTA REGION. That is not distance_to_boundary, which returns the nearest surface at ANY coordinate level. It needs the boundary of the cell that DECLARED delta -- i.e. the level in GeometryPath at which tracking was set. So locate should report that level alongside the method, and distance_to_boundary needs a variant that stops at a named level.

That is a small, well-defined addition to op-867c.1's work, not a new subsystem.

SECOND ITEM, independent: the delta path has no Tally at all (zero hits in keff_delta.rs). Under this design that mostly solves itself, since tallying happens in the shared part of the loop -- but it needs checking that a delta flight's track-length contribution is scored on the RIGHT segments. A delta flight crosses several materials virtually before its real collision, so scoring must be per sub-flight, not once per real collision.

title: Phase 1.4: one transport loop replacing the two drivers
